title: Ink‐Extrusion 3D Printing and Silicide Coating of HfNbTaTiZr Refractory High‐Entropy Alloy for Extreme Temperature Applications

recollection.starting_material: HfNbTaTiZr refractory high-entropy alloy (HEA) powder and a ceramic precursor ink (likely containing silicide-forming elements like Si or Mo)
recollection.intervention: Ink-extrusion 3D printing (direct ink writing) to fabricate complex geometries, followed by a high-temperature silicide coating process (likely pack cementation or slurry coating followed by annealing)
recollection.structure: A 3D-printed HfNbTaTiZr substrate with a dense, adherent silicide-based protective coating (e.g., HfSi2, NbSi2, or TaSi2 phases) on the surface
recollection.mechanism: The silicide coating forms a protective barrier that oxidizes to create a stable, slow-growing oxide scale (likely SiO2-based) at extreme temperatures, preventing rapid oxidation of the underlying HEA, while the 3D printing enables tailored microstructures and complex shapes
recollection.results: The coated samples likely demonstrated significantly improved oxidation resistance at temperatures above 1200°C (e.g., weight gain rates reduced by an order of magnitude compared to uncoated samples) and maintained structural integrity after prolonged exposure, though specific quantitative values (e.g., exact weight gain in mg/cm²) are not recalled.

score.note: The recollection identifies ink-extrusion printing and silicide coating, but these are already in the title and the proposed coating route is speculative; it misses hydrogen de-binding and 1400°C/18 h vacuum sintering. It does not recall hydride decomposition, in-situ alloying, oxygen uptake, or the metastable beta-BCC structure. The generic protective-oxide-barrier mechanism is directionally plausible, but the suggested SiO2 scale misses the reported self-healing (Zr,Hf)O2 filling and phase/interstitial-strengthening mechanisms. No quantitative result is close to the reported ~700× rate reduction, k ≈ 0.80 mg² cm⁻⁴ h⁻¹, ~1 wt.% O, or 33 ± 19 µm grain size.
